name: page-peel
title: Page Peel
description: A dog-ear in the corner that peels the whole page back along a real fold to show what is drawn underneath.

props.description: Wraps the page and draws the corner, the folded flap and the underside.

props.name: underside
props.description: What the peel reveals. Give it its own ground color.

props.name: scope
props.description: Peel the window or the nearest box.

props.name: openAt
props.description: Share of the page peeled past which a release opens fully, about 60% of the diagonal. Below it the page settles back. A fast flick decides on its own.

props.name: undersideLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the revealed region.
A native button that opens and closes the peel. Extends every button prop except onClick and type.

accessibility: The corner and the open fold are pointer only. PagePeelTrigger gives keyboard and screen reader users the same toggle, with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Open, the page is inert, focus moves to the underside and Escape closes it. Focus returns to the trigger.
Closed, the underside is inert and hidden from assistive tech.

animation.trigger: Pointer enters the corner or the open fold
Drag the corner, or the fold when open
animation.reducedMotion: No fold. A tap opens or closes.

animation.timing: Critically damped spring seeded with the release velocity, about 500 ms, no overshoot

docs: Wrap your page in <PagePeel underside={<YourUnderside />}>. The default scope is the viewport: the dog-ear sits in the bottom-right corner of the window. Use scope="container" to peel a single box. Put <PagePeelTrigger /> anywhere inside for a keyboard path.
